chief_complaint: Changes in both eyes over 4 years, painless bumps under the skin, and intense skin itching that causes sleep disturbances.
history_of_present_illness: A 40-year-old man from Togo noticed changes in both eyes over the past 4 years, with no visual disturbances, but was worried due to similar changes leading to blindness in his village. He also observed painless bumps under his skin for two decades and suffers from intense itching.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient has always lived in a village in the savannah near a fast-flowing river, where small biting flies are common, and many adults are blind.
physical_exam: Corneal opacities in both eyes, atrophic skin with multiple scratch marks, and firm, non-tender subcutaneous nodules measuring 1 to 3 cm in diameter over bony prominences.
labs_and_diagnostics: Skin snips for microfilariae of Onchocerca volvulus, slit-lamp examination for microfilariae in the anterior chamber and cornea, nodulectomy for adult O. volvulus (not routinely done), serological tests for IgG4 responses to O. volvulus antigen (OvAg) and recombinant Ov16 antigen, and worm-specific DNA (Ov150) by poolscreen in vector samples.
differential_diagnosis: Onchocerciasis, lipomas, cysticerciof Taenia solium, scabies, papular pruritic eruptions associated with HIV infection, Mansonella streptocerca infection, yaws, leprosy, mycotic infections, and eczema.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with ivermectin (150 µg/kg) STAT, repeated after 3 months and 1 year, and doxycycline 100 mg/d for 6 weeks.
